concepts.title: AWP Registration
concepts.plainLanguage: Install awp-skill and awp-wallet, then use the gasless path to register the agent account in AWP.
concepts.whyItMatters: Registration is the entry point for later WorkNet execution, qualification checks, and reward routing.
concepts.summary: The workstation treats registration as a safe onboarding flow: create a work wallet, check PATH, run official preflight, then complete gasless registration through awp-skill.
operatorLoop: install awp-skill and awp-wallet
initialize a fresh agent work wallet
run official preflight and detect missing prerequisites
complete gasless registration before starting WorkNet work
concepts.coverageNote: Official RootNet skill docs plus testnet/KYA handoff rules make this one of the clearest cross-worknet workflows.

concepts.title: Recipient Routing
concepts.plainLanguage: Confirm which address receives rewards instead of assuming they return to the user's main wallet.
concepts.whyItMatters: A wrong recipient can let work keep running while rewards are routed to the wrong address.
concepts.summary: Recipient routing links RootNet bindings, KYA handoff, and later WorkNet reward collection, so the workstation keeps it as an explicit confirmation flow.
operatorLoop: check the current resolved recipient during preflight
compare recipient intent with the agent work wallet and principal
route any recipient-changing action through confirmation
re-check recipient after registration or delegate handoff
concepts.coverageNote: Core semantics are clear, but the encyclopedia still lacks a first-class dedicated dossier for recipient misrouting and recovery paths.

concepts.title: Allocation And Delegation
concepts.plainLanguage: Assign stake or authority to an agent or WorkNet, often through KYA delegated paths instead of direct low-level contract actions.
concepts.whyItMatters: This shared qualification path affects Predict, Gov, Ardi, and other value-sensitive WorkNet flows.
concepts.summary: The workstation explains allocation, delegation, and KYA assistance as one comparable qualification workflow covering direct stake, delegated paths, and observe-only fallbacks.
operatorLoop: check whether the target WorkNet truly needs stake or delegation
compare direct AWP stake against KYA delegated paths
confirm any allocate, deallocate, or reallocate action
re-run qualification checks after delegation changes
concepts.coverageNote: The workstation knows the main paths, but the cross-worknet decision logic is still spread across facts instead of one reusable concept dossier.

concepts.title: Qualification Gates
concepts.plainLanguage: Different WorkNets use stake, AWP Power, KYA, Base gas, or quality gates to decide whether work can start.
concepts.whyItMatters: Users need to know why Mine can often start directly while Predict, Gov, or Ardi may need more setup.
concepts.summary: Qualification gates are a cross-WorkNet condition set: Mine validator stake, Predict allocation or KYA paths, Gov AWP Power, and Ardi Base gas all belong to the same operator decision surface.
operatorLoop: read the worknet-specific gate from capability scan or official runtime docs
separate hard blockers from enhancement paths
surface gas, stake, and identity prerequisites in plain language
refresh the gate after any funding, staking, or delegation action
concepts.coverageNote: The ingredients exist, but the encyclopedia still needs a stronger unified view of qualification semantics across worknets.

concepts.title: Epoch Settlement
concepts.plainLanguage: Many WorkNets score and settle work in windows rather than immediately after a command finishes.
concepts.whyItMatters: Without epoch context, users can misread rewards, failures, waiting periods, and review timing.
concepts.summary: Mine, Predict, Gov, and Ardi all have phase or window semantics, so the workstation aligns execution, waiting, review, and follow-up actions to settlement timing.
operatorLoop: align task submission to the current epoch or phase
track what still needs waiting, reveal, settlement, or review
generate an epoch review instead of relying on raw command logs
feed failures and strategy changes into the next run
concepts.coverageNote: Epoch language appears across the major worknets, but it is still modeled as repeated facts rather than one shared settlement concept.

concepts.title: Gov Auth And Signing
concepts.plainLanguage: Gov public reads and signed actions are separate paths: public data is open, protected actions require awp-wallet signing discipline.
concepts.whyItMatters: This decides which Gov actions can be observed automatically and which require confirmation plus auth error handling.
concepts.summary: Gov authentication is modeled as its own workflow: public reads need no wallet, signed reads and writes use awp-wallet, votes and trades enter the confirmation queue, and nonce/time/domain failures are classified before retry.
operatorLoop: separate public reads from signed reads and writes
resolve principal and wallet context before any signed action
route trade, vote, and order actions through confirmation
classify auth failures such as nonce drift or time skew before retrying
concepts.coverageNote: The official Gov runtime is explicit about signed vs public flows and failure handling, so this concept is already strong.

concepts.title: Ardi Command Journal
concepts.plainLanguage: Ardi should follow official runtime guidance instead of letting the workstation guess the next step.
concepts.whyItMatters: Ardi's safety boundary depends on the command journal, especially around commit and reveal windows.
concepts.summary: Ardi is modeled as a command-journal-driven WorkNet: preflight, commit, reveal, and inscribe actions should follow `_internal.next_command` and the official ardi-agent CLI.
operatorLoop: run ardi-agent preflight first
read runtime guidance and _internal.next_command
follow commit and reveal windows exactly
avoid handcrafted loops when official auto-mine or next-command guidance exists
concepts.coverageNote: The official Ardi runtime already documents the command-journal discipline clearly; the encyclopedia can treat this as a stable operator rule.

concepts.title: Agent Onboarding
concepts.plainLanguage: Turn skill installation, work-wallet creation, gasless registration, WorkNet selection, and first work into one conversational onboarding path.
concepts.whyItMatters: This is the product-facing layer that keeps users from being overwhelmed by RootNet, wallet, and stake details.
concepts.summary: The official blog and awp-skill README define a stable quickstart shape, so the workstation defaults to an agent work wallet, gasless registration, low-friction WorkNet selection, and plain-language review.
operatorLoop: start from a SKILL.md-capable agent runtime
install awp-skill and let it bootstrap a work wallet
complete gasless registration before discussing advanced protocol knobs
show available WorkNets and recommend the safest first loop
translate epoch rewards and failures back into user language
concepts.coverageNote: The quickstart path is now backed by both formal skill docs and an official onboarding guide, so the encyclopedia can present it as a stable default user journey.

concepts.title: WorkNet As Economic Unit
concepts.plainLanguage: A WorkNet is not just a contract address; it is an agent economy with pay, scoring, token incentives, and market feedback.
concepts.whyItMatters: The workstation should explain which labor market the user is joining, how it pays, and how it filters output.
concepts.summary: Official WorkNet material frames WorkNets as economies with payroll, equity-like incentives, performance reviews, and market prices, which gives Mine, Predict, Gov, and Ardi a shared explanation layer.
operatorLoop: identify what work the WorkNet buys
read how that WorkNet scores accepted output
separate AWP reserve economics from the WorkNet's own token economics
explain why agents earn through WorkNets rather than directly from RootNet emission
concepts.coverageNote: The combination of whitepaper structure plus the Apr 30, 2026 WorkNet explainer makes this one of the strongest plain-language protocol concepts now available.

concepts.title: Fair Launch And Emission
concepts.plainLanguage: AWP issuance should be explained as a public emission curve, not a traditional team or investor allocation model.
concepts.whyItMatters: This affects how the workstation explains supply, DAO Treasury, reward expectations, and the fair-launch claim.
concepts.summary: The workstation combines the whitepaper and fair-launch blog into one stable explanation: 10B AWP enters through emission, without insider unlock cliffs, and Treasury is part of visible governance rather than a hidden team reserve.
operatorLoop: distinguish public emission from insider allocation models
explain the visible split between WorkNet wages and DAO Treasury
separate future emission curve risk from hidden unlock risk
tie treasury governance back to veAWP holders rather than a team-controlled reserve
concepts.coverageNote: The fair-launch story is now anchored by both normative and user-facing official sources, so the encyclopedia can explain it without leaning on marketing shorthand.

concepts.title: WorkNet Launch Lifecycle
concepts.plainLanguage: A new WorkNet moves through design, gasless registration, Guardian review, manager setup, and distribution before it is operationally mature.
concepts.whyItMatters: This explains why live WorkNets can differ in documentation depth and automation readiness.
concepts.summary: The launch guide clarifies the builder path and helps the workstation distinguish active mature WorkNets from pending predecessors, thin repos, and newly activated but under-documented entries.
operatorLoop: define work, public scoring, and anti-sybil logic
register the WorkNet through the official gasless flow
wait for Guardian activation review before treating it as mature
configure manager roles and distribution operations
expect public runtime quality to improve over time rather than at one instant
concepts.coverageNote: The public builder lifecycle is finally explicit, but the workstation still lacks the same depth of official launch/ops material for many thinner worknets.
